reason: E1 supports the premise that limited atom mobility during synthesis of multi-element nanoparticles promotes random, non-equilibrium configurations, but it does not provide evidence linking this to local lattice strain heterogeneity, spatial variation in melting points, or a broadened melting transition. E2 discusses synthesis methods for HEA nanoparticles but offers no data on thermal behavior, premelting, or melting transitions. The key mechanistic premises connecting configurational entropy to heterogeneous melting are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Adding more elements promotes a more random nanoparticle due to limited atom mobility during synthesis
Limited atom mobility during synthesis traps non-equilibrium configurations in multi-element nanoparticles
The resulting random, multi-element distribution creates local lattice strain heterogeneity
Local lattice strain heterogeneity leads to spatial variation in effective melting points within a single nanoparticle
